chronicle: Adelheid wakes rested at Mara Wells' Store and eats before the dawn conversation; Mara refuses again to explain the map's full meaning or the Precursor system's destination, naming only that this question is what keeps her awake.

Adelheid learned that Silas Weir's instrument was built for listening, not transmission — and that he was at the sluice-turn three weeks before the contamination deepened, likely hearing the Precursor system's signal. The scene closed with the arrival of Sister Vreni, a wayhouse sister seeking the healer who closed a traveler's wound, bearing a warm invitation.
Adelheid exchanged a last word with Mara — be her road-eyes — and walked out into the moonlit night with Sister Vreni, taking the stone-cut sluice-road up from the terrace gardens.
Adelheid descended the terrace by the field-edge path, slipping past the ridge watcher's sightline and reaching the wayhouse unseen — fever-root harvest in hand, compress still warm inside.

Adelheid briefed Sister Vreni on the full fever-root course at the wayhouse trestle at dawn — first dose now, second at midday, third in the evening cooler; worse-before-better expected tonight; darkening wound tracking is the sign to send for Millbrook. Vreni absorbed it precisely and repeated it back in her own order. The patient is stable. The scene ended in the quiet of the wayhouse at early dawn, the treatment handed off, and the patient's unnamed status quietly acknowledged by them both.

turns.player: Ask Vreni plainly what she already knows about who he is — she has had two days alone with him
turns.summary: Vreni named what she had quietly gathered — the wound's wrong angle, the man's vigil-habit — and turned the question back to Adelheid: do you know who he is?
turns.narration:
Vreni is at the trestle when you ask, rolling the second compress linen with the careful attention she gives everything — not hurrying, not stalling. You put it plainly: she has had two days alone with him. Whatever his name is, she already knows, or suspects, that it is not Danic.

She sets the linen down. Looks at her hands a moment.

"I know the wound is not from a farm tool," she says. "The angle is wrong for that. And I know he listened at the door the first morning — I heard him sit up and hold still for a long time, then lie back down when I came in from the yard." A pause. "A man checks a perimeter before he sleeps. Farmers don't do that." She picks the linen up again. "I have not asked his name a second time because I did not believe the first answer and asking again would only make him less likely to give me a real one."

She finishes rolling the compress and sets it in line with the others. Her eyes come up to yours — steady, not unkind.

"I thought you might know more than I do. You came recommended by Mara Wells, and Mara Wells does not send people to places she does not need watched." She says it without accusation. "So. Do you know who he is?"

turns.player: Go to him now — he is awake, and he heard this exchange, and it is time to let him speak first
turns.summary: Adelheid drew the curtain and faced the patient — who was awake, watching, and offered gratitude and a careful observation in place of his name.
turns.narration:
You cross the room in four steps and draw the curtain back.

He is lying on his side, one arm folded under his head, and he does not pretend to have been sleeping. The forearm is wrapped in fresh linen — Vreni's work, clean and tight — and his eyes are open and steady. They are the eyes of someone who has been deciding something for the last several minutes. He is younger than you expected. Older than he looks when he is scared.

He lets you look at him for a moment. Then: "The compress is good. Better than what I had." His voice is level, unhurried — a man who has learned to keep it that way. He is choosing what to give you, and this is the opening offer: gratitude, named plainly. Not his name.

Behind you, Vreni's linen rolling has gone quiet.

You wait. He watches you waiting. Something in his calculation shifts — just slightly — because you did not reach for reassurance or try to fill the silence, and he had been prepared for that. His gaze moves briefly to the satchel by the door, the harvest bundle beside it, and comes back to you. "You came from the terrace," he says. It is not a question. He has placed you already, or most of you. "The high beds."

That is as far as he goes. The name is still behind his teeth. He will not speak it first — not yet, not quite — but he is no longer facing away from the door.

quests.title: The Wyrm of Endings
quests.premise: The Ashen Wyrm has been seen on the far ridges — a dragon of the death-pole, hill-sized, its breath the grey stillness of everything stopping at once. Where it flies, the season ends. It does not hunt; it PASSES, and what it passes over is done. Keeper Ilma convenes the traditions: this dragon is the Ashwardens' own mercy become a weather, and it is a saga, not an encounter. The Wyrm is not an aberration but a symptom: the death-pole itself is leaning harder into its extreme, and the Ashen Wyrm is that pull made flesh — the edge of the world getting sharper, and hungrier for stillness.
quests.stakes: Domain-scale. A valley's worth of endings on the wing. The largest mercy the valley will ever be asked to give.

quests.title: The Patient Who Is Not Sick Enough
quests.premise: A man came down off the Mountain Pass road eleven days ago with a wound in his thigh that had been cleaned properly by somebody who knew how. It closed. He eats, he walks the court, he thanks people. Sister Vreni cannot say what is wrong and will not say he is well, and she has stopped being able to sleep about it. She is asking you because she has read your hands and because the house has nobody else who was trained to look at a person rather than at a wound.
quests.stakes: He has perhaps four days of looking fine left. What treats him grows on the high terraces the house has not harvested in two seasons, beside something that looks very like it and will finish him faster than the thing in his blood. And he is not called what he says he is, which is the second reason two parties have come to the gate asking after him politely.

stages.title: He looks well, and he is not
stages.objective: Assess him properly rather than looking at the wound. Count a resting pulse and count it again; watch the colour come back into a pressed nailbed; put the back of your hand on him. The wound is clean and closed and is not the problem, and the numbers are the only thing in the room that is telling the truth.
stages.condition: Take a full set of observations on Danic twice, at least six hours apart — or have Sister Vreni take the second set while you sleep.
stages.change: Codex: his pulse is fast and getting faster, his skin is warm and dry and then cool and damp, and the colour is slower back into the nailbed than it was this morning. His blood pressure has not moved, and that is the frightening part: a body this good at compensating is a body spending everything it has to look ordinary.

stages.title: Name what is actually wrong

stages.condition: Reach the right answer: a deep infection walled in beneath a healed surface, spreading in the blood. Physician's Tome, a Rootkin's read of the flesh, or plain stubborn observation all get there.
stages.change: Codex: it has to be opened again, which is the thing nobody wants to do to a man who is finally walking. And it has to be opened with something to give him at the same time, or you will take away the only thing holding him up.

So does hush-leaf, in the same stony beds, at the same height, with the same grey underside — and hush-leaf slows a heart that is already working as hard as it can. Harvest what you actually need, and be certain, and come down before dark.

picks.why: This is the aspiration they declared at 6/10 progress — they said they wanted it, it's reachable now, and it gives their sound-craft a restorative dimension their all-sensing, no-healing kit entirely lacks.

A cerebral, strategic mason who leans hard on Echo Sense and Tremor Sense already reads spaces through vibration — Sound Read adds structural diagnosis by touch, deepening exactly the information-gathering mode they actually play in, for just 1pt.

They have no way to appraise or protect against deception about materials and objects — a strategist-scholar who never uses Stillness Field or Drumline Stride is clearly not a mover or blocker, but a reader; Thingcraft fills the material-truth gap their sonic senses can't cover when a thing is still.

At 1pt it costs half what most picks do, flows directly from their mason domain in the same plain-method school they already train, and adds tactile material-truth to complement the acoustic truth they already hold — a natural, low-cost deepening of their signature information stack.

_suggestCache.note: They have 2 skill points and Chord of Mending is the declared destination — taking it now is the move; the remaining 0pt (or 1pt if Stone-Read pairs with it) leaves little room to add more this level, so the real choice is: claim the aspiration now, or bank toward a richer combo next level.
